answer: The beacon anchors a key only once that key's own chain holds J shale — units of judged work the key itself performed and signed in sequence, non-transferable and worthless to any other chain. The beacon certifies only S shale per epoch across all comers, so an attacker queuing k clones finds each vertex must earn its own J and the last one waits about k·J/S epochs: every added vertex pushes the queue back, a bill in elapsed attested epochs that grows per head and cannot be split or parallelized past the beacon. Break: the beacon inflating S clears the backlog.
